verses.en: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.
verses.pt: E tendo sobrevivido, então souberam que a ilha se chamava Malta.
verses.en_web: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.
verses.en_bbe: And when we were safe, we made the discovery that the island was named Melita.

verses.en: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
verses.pt: E os nativos demonstraram para conosco uma benevolência incomum; porque, tendo acendido uma fogueira, recolheram a nós todos, por causa da chuva que estava caindo, e por causa do frio.
verses.en_web: The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire, and received us all, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
verses.en_bbe: And the simple people living there were uncommonly kind to us, for they made a fire for us, and took us in, because it was raining and cold.

verses.en: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
verses.pt: E tendo Paulo recolhido uma quantidade de gravetos, e pondo-os no fogo, saiu uma víbora do calor, e fixou os dentes na mão dele.
verses.en_web: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
verses.en_bbe: But when Paul had got some sticks together and put them on the fire, a snake came out, because of the heat, and gave him a bite on the hand.

verses.en: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.
verses.pt: E quando os nativos vieram o animal pendurado na mão dele, disseram uns aos outros: Certamente este homem é assassino, ao qual, tendo sobrevivido do mar, a justiça não o deixa viver.
verses.en_web: When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet Justice has not allowed to live.”
verses.en_bbe: And when the people saw it hanging on his hand, they said to one another, Without doubt this man has put someone to death, and though he has got safely away from the sea, God will not let him go on living.

verses.en: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.
verses.pt: Porém, ele, tendo sacudido o animal ao fogo, sofreu nenhum mal.
verses.en_web: However he shook off the creature into the fire, and wasn’t harmed.
verses.en_bbe: But shaking off the beast into the fire, he got no damage.

verses.en: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.
verses.pt: E eles esperavam que ele fosse inchar, ou cair morto de repente. Mas tendo esperado muito, e vendo que nenhum incômodo tinha lhe sobrevindo, mudaram de opinião, e diziam que ele era um deus.
verses.en_web: But they expected that he would have swollen or fallen down dead suddenly, but when they watched for a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.
verses.en_bbe: But they had the idea that they would see him becoming ill, or suddenly falling down dead; but after waiting a long time, and seeing that no damage came to him, changing their opinion, they said he was a god.

verses.en: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.
verses.pt: E perto daquele mesmo lugar o homem mais importante da ilha, por nome Públio, tinha algumas propriedades; o qual nos recebeu e nos hospedou por três dias gentilmente.
verses.en_web: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us, and courteously entertained us for three days.
verses.en_bbe: Now near that place there was some land, the property of the chief man of the island, who was named Publius; who very kindly took us into his house as his guests for three days.

verses.en: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.
verses.pt: E aconteceu que o pai de Públio estava de cama, doente de febres e disenteria; ao qual Paulo entrou, e tendo orado, pôs as mãos sobre ele, e o curou.
verses.en_web: The father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery. Paul entered in to him, prayed, and laying his hands on him, healed him.
verses.en_bbe: And the father of Publius was ill, with a disease of the stomach; to whom Paul went, and put his hands on him, with prayer, and made him well.

verses.en: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:
verses.pt: Tendo então isto acontecido, também vieram a ele outros que tinham enfermidades, e foram curados;
verses.en_web: Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came, and were cured.
verses.en_bbe: And when this took place, all the others in the island who had diseases came and were made well.

verses.en: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.
verses.pt: Os quais nos honraram com muitas honras; e estando nós para navegar, nos entregaram as coisas necessárias.
verses.en_web: They also honored us with many honors, and when we sailed, they put on board the things that we needed.
verses.en_bbe: Then they gave us great honour, and, when we went away, they put into the ship whatever things we were in need of.

verses.en: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.
verses.pt: E três meses depois, nós partimos em um navio de Alexandria, que tinha passado o inverno na ilha; o qual tinha como símbolo os gêmeos Castor e Pólux.
verses.en_web: After three months, we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose sign was “The Twin Brothers.”
verses.en_bbe: And after three months we went to sea in a ship of Alexandria sailing under the sign of the Dioscuri, which had been at the island for the winter.

verses.en: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.
verses.pt: E chegando a Siracusa, ficamos ali três dias.
verses.en_web: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
verses.en_bbe: And going into the harbour at Syracuse, we were waiting there for three days.

verses.en: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:
verses.pt: De onde, tendo indo ao redor da costa, chegamos a Régio; e um dia depois, ventando ao sul, viemos o segundo dia a Putéoli.
verses.en_web: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,
verses.en_bbe: And from there, going about in a curve, we came to Rhegium: and after one day a south wind came up and on the day after we came to Puteoli:

verses.en: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.
verses.pt: Onde, tendo achado alguns irmãos, eles nos rogaram que ficássemos com eles por sete dias; e assim viemos a Roma.
verses.en_web: where we found brothers, and were entreated to stay with them for seven days. So we came to Rome.
verses.en_bbe: Where we came across some of the brothers, who kept us with them for seven days; and so we came to Rome.

verses.en: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii Forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.
verses.pt: E os irmãos, ao ouvirem notícias sobre nós, desde lá nos saíram ao encontro até a praça de Ápio, e as três tavernas; e Paulo, tendo os visto, agradeceu a Deus, e tomou coragem.
verses.en_web: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God, and took courage.
verses.en_bbe: And the brothers, when they had news of us, came out from town as far as Appii Forum and the Three Taverns to have a meeting with us: and Paul, seeing them, gave praise to God and took heart.

verses.en: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.
verses.pt: E quando chegamos a Roma, o centurião entregou os prisioneiros ao chefe da guarda, mas a Paulo foi permitido morar por si mesmo à parte, junto com o soldado que o guardava.
verses.en_web: When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.
verses.en_bbe: And when we came into Rome, they let Paul have a house for himself and the armed man who kept watch over him.

verses.en: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
verses.pt: E aconteceu que, três dias depois, Paulo chamou juntos os chefes dos judeus; e ao se reunirem, disse-lhes: Homens irmãos, tendo eu nada feito contra o povo, ou contra os costumes dos pais, mesmo assim eu vim preso desde Jerusalém, entregue em mãos dos romanos.
verses.en_web: After three days Paul called together those who were the leaders of the Jews. When they had come together, he said to them, “I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people, or the customs of our fathers, still was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,
verses.en_bbe: Then after three days he sent for the chief men of the Jews: and when they had come together, he said to them, My brothers, though I had done nothing against the people or the ways of our fathers, I was given, a prisoner from Jerusalem, into the hands of the Romans.

verses.en: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.
verses.pt: Os quais, tendo me investigado, queriam me soltar, por não haver em mim nenhum crime de morte.
verses.en_web: who, when they had examined me, desired to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me.
verses.en_bbe: Who, when they had put questions to me, were ready to let me go free, because there was no cause of death in me.

verses.en: But when the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.
verses.pt: Mas os judeus, dizendo em contrário, eu fui forçado a apelar a César; mas não como que eu tenha que acusar a minha nação.
verses.en_web: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything about which to accuse my nation.
verses.en_bbe: But when the Jews made protest against it, I had to put my cause into Caesar's hands; not because I have anything to say against my nation.

verses.en: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you, and to speak with you: because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.
verses.pt: Então por esta causa eu vos chamei até mim, para vos ver e falar; porque pela esperança de Israel eu estou agora preso nesta corrente.
verses.en_web: For this cause therefore I asked to see you and to speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.”
verses.en_bbe: But for this reason I sent for you, to see and have talk with you: for because of the hope of Israel I am in these chains.

verses.en: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judaea concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.
verses.pt: Mas eles lhe disseram: Nós nem recebemos cartas da Judeia relacionadas a ti, nem algum dos irmãos, tendo vindo aqui, tem nos informado ou falado de ti algum mal.
verses.en_web: They said to him, “We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brothers come here and report or speak any evil of you.
verses.en_bbe: And they said to him, We have not had letters from Judaea about you, and no one of the brothers has come to us here to give an account or say any evil about you.

verses.en: But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.
verses.pt: Mas nós queríamos ouvir de ti o que tu pensas; porque, quanto a esta seita, conhecemos que em todo lugar há quem fale contra ela.
verses.en_web: But we desire to hear from you what you think. For, as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.”
verses.en_bbe: But we have a desire to give hearing to your opinion: for as to this form of religion, we have knowledge that in all places it is attacked.

verses.en: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.
verses.pt: E tendo eles lhe determinado um dia, muitos vieram até onde ele estava morando; aos quais ele declarava e dava testemunho do Reino de Deus; e procurava persuadi-los quanto a Jesus, tanto pela Lei de Moisés, como pelos profetas, desde a manhã até a tarde.
verses.en_web: When they had appointed him a day, many people came to him at his lodging. He explained to them, testifying about God’s Kingdom, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning until evening.
verses.en_bbe: And when a day had been fixed, they came to his house in great numbers; and he gave them teaching, giving witness to the kingdom of God, and having discussions with them about Jesus, from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning till evening.

verses.en: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.
verses.pt: E alguns criam nas coisas que ele dizia; mas outros não criam.
verses.en_web: Some believed the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.
verses.en_bbe: And some were in agreement with what he said, but some had doubts.

verses.en: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,
verses.pt: E estando discordantes entre si, despediram-se, tendo Paulo disto esta palavra: O Espírito Santo corretamente falou a nossos pais por meio de Isaías o profeta,
verses.en_web: When they didn’t agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one word, “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah, the prophet, to our fathers,
verses.en_bbe: And they went away, for there was a division among them after Paul had said this one thing: Well did the Holy Spirit say by the prophet Isaiah to your fathers,

verses.en: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:
verses.pt: Dizendo: Vai a este povo, e dize: De fato ouvireis, mas de maneira nenhuma entendereis; e de fato vereis, mas de maneira nenhuma enxergareis.
verses.en_web: saying, ‘Go to this people, and say, in hearing, you will hear, but will in no way understand. In seeing, you will see, but will in no way perceive.
verses.en_bbe: Go to this people and say, Though you give ear, you will not get knowledge; and seeing, you will see, but the sense will not be clear to you:

verses.en: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
verses.pt: Porque o coração deste povo está insensível, seus ouvidos ouvem com dificuldade, e seus olhos estão fechados; para que em maneira nenhuma vejam com os olhos, nem ouçam com os ouvidos, nem entendam com o coração, e se convertam, e eu os cure.
verses.en_web: For this people’s heart has grown callous. Their ears are dull of hearing. Their eyes they have closed. Lest they should see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and would turn again, and I would heal them.’
verses.en_bbe: For the heart of this people has become fat and their ears are slow in hearing and their eyes are shut; for fear that they might see with their eyes and give hearing with their ears and become wise in their hearts and be turned again to me, so that I might make them well.

verses.en: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.
verses.pt: Portanto seja conhecido por vós que a salvação de Deus foi enviada aos gentios; e eles a ouvirão.
verses.en_web: “Be it known therefore to you, that the salvation of God is sent to the nations, and they will listen.”
verses.en_bbe: Be certain, then, that the salvation of God is sent to the Gentiles, and they will give hearing.

verses.en: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.
verses.pt: E havendo ele dito isto, os judeus foram embora, havendo entre eles grande discussão.
verses.en_web: When he had said these words, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves.

verses.en: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,
verses.pt: E Paulo ficou dois anos inteiros em sua própria casa alugada; e recebia a todos quantos vinham a ele;
verses.en_web: Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented house, and received all who were coming to him,
verses.en_bbe: And for the space of two years, Paul was living in the house of which he had the use, and had talk with all those who went in to see him,

verses.en: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
verses.pt: Pregando o Reino de Deus, e ensinando com ousadia a doutrina do Senhor Jesus Cristo, sem impedimento algum.
verses.en_web: preaching God’s Kingdom, and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.
verses.en_bbe: Preaching the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ without fear, and no orders were given that he was not to do so.
